record.original_question: Do the surjective pairing axioms D1(D x y) = x, D2(D x y) = y, and D(D1 x)(D2 x) = x conservatively extend lambda-beta-eta conversion on pure untyped lambda terms? More generally, is surjective pairing conservative over every lambda theory or extension of Combinatory Logic, or are there theories for which conservative extension by surjective pairing fails?

evidence.quote: Does surjective pairing conservatively extend λβη-conversion?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Work in the untyped lambda calculus with λβη-conversion. Extend the syntax by three constants D, D₁, D₂ (surjective pairing) and impose the equational axioms

  (SP1)  D₁(D x y) = x,
  (SP2)  D₂(D x y) = y,
  (SP3)  D(D₁ x)(D₂ x) = x.

Let λβη+SP denote the resulting equational theory. The conservative extension question asks: for any two pure λ-terms M, N (containing none of D, D₁, D₂), does

  λβη+SP ⊢ M = N   ⟹   λβη ⊢ M = N ?

More generally, given an arbitrary lambda theory T (an equational extension of λβ on pure λ-terms), or an extension of Combinatory Logic, is the extension of T by the surjective pairing axioms above always conservative over T, or do there exist such theories T over which adding surjective pairing fails to be conservative?
artifact.status_search_result: The core question — conservativity of surjective pairing over λβη on pure λ-terms — was answered affirmatively (Støvring, "Extending the Extensional Lambda Calculus with Surjective Pairing is Conservative", LMCS 2006/2007), confirming a long-standing conjecture of Klop and de Vrijer. However, the more general question of characterizing exactly which lambda theories or extensions of Combinatory Logic admit conservative extension by surjective pairing (and constructing or ruling out counterexamples) is not fully resolved in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Extending the Extensional Lambda Calculus with Surjective Pairing is Conservative
status_evidence.snippet: We answer Klop and de Vrijer's question whether adding surjective-pairing axioms to the extensional lambda calculus yields a conservative extension. The answer is positive.
status_evidence.claim: Conservativity of surjective pairing over λβη is established.

status_evidence.title: Unique normal forms for lambda calculus with surjective pairing (Klop, de Vrijer)
status_evidence.snippet: Lambda calculus extended with constants π, π0, π1 and surjective pairing axioms; reduction lacks confluence but normal forms are unique.
status_evidence.claim: Background on the λπ theory and its reduction-theoretic anomalies.
